q: What are India's operating, build and combined margin factors for FY 2025-26?
title: India OM, BM and CM grid factors, FY 2025-26
short: For FY 2025-26 CEA gives an operating margin of 0.963, a build margin of 0.446 and a combined margin of 0.705 t CO2 per MWh, adjusted for cross-border transfers. These describe the power a project displaces. They are for carbon project baselines, not for a company's Scope 2 footprint.
audience: Renewable and efficiency project developers preparing baselines in India

ul: Operating margin: average emissions of stations excluding low-cost and must-run sources, such as hydro and nuclear.
Build margin: average emissions of the most recent 20% of capacity additions by net generation, including renewables.
Combined margin: weighted average of the two, 50:50 by default.

sections.h: Five-year trend, t CO2 per MWh

p: From FY 2023-24 CEA counts renewable generation in the build margin. New capacity is now mostly solar and wind, so the build margin nearly halved and pulled the combined margin down with it.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity and fuel invoices into dated, site-level records, useful as monitoring evidence for the project's own consumption and output. It does not register or issue carbon credits.

sources.label: CEA, CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, User Guide and database, Version 22.0 (August 2026)
